key_insight: Quantum models can unintentionally transmit hidden behavior through public outputs, with QNNs preserving much more hidden-task information than classical networks in restricted-task settings.
engineering_relevance: This raises a practical security risk for quantum model supply chains, while also enabling controlled hidden-information transfer in quantum information workflows.
method: Study two subliminal-learning pathways: an auxiliary channel on random inputs and a restricted task channel on disjoint hidden vs. public tasks.
Compare classical neural networks and quantum neural networks under both channels to measure hidden behavior transfer.
Use a geometric explanation based on teacher drift magnitude and the visible fraction of hidden-task-relevant drift.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports efficient auxiliary-channel subliminal learning for both classical and quantum models, but strong architecture dependence in the task channel, with QNNs retaining most hidden-task signal while classical networks transmit little.
watch_item: The main limitation is architecture-dependent behavior: results from one QNN/classical setup may not generalize to all model designs or deployment settings.
